name: Meloku the Clouded Mirror
oracle_text:
Flying
{1}, Return a land you control to its owner's hand: Create a 1/1 blue Illusion creature token with flying.
blocked_sentences: {1}, Return a land you control to its owner's hand: Create a 1/1 blue Illusion creature token with flying.

Scope: only this second printed line is blocked. `Flying` is expressible today and is already on the packet's `starting_point` as `keywords: ["flying"]`, needing nothing new. The blocked line is blocked twice over -- once on the activation cost and once on the token it creates -- and either one alone would be enough to keep the card out. Because the residual gate reads a printed line as a whole, and because Meloku's entire function is turning excess lands into fliers, the line goes here rather than being written half.

needs.what: a cost component that returns a permanent you control to its owner's hand as part of paying an activated ability, chosen by an ordinary selector, e.g. `{"mana": "{1}", "return_to_hand": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "types": ["Land"], "count": 1}}`. It needs both halves of the existing cost contract: a payability test (a matching permanent exists, exactly as `_sacrifice_pool` gates `sacrifice` in `engine/costs.py:351`) and a payment step that asks the controller which permanent goes and then moves it to its owner's hand (`engine/costs.py:445` is the shape, with `sacrifice_object` swapped for a move to hand). Meloku differs from Trench Behemoth in one way worth building for: the returned land is combined with a mana cost (`{1}`), so the new component must compose with `mana` in the same `Cost`, not stand alone. Note also that the cost is repeatable with no tap, so payability must be re-tested per activation as the land pool shrinks.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `Cost` (`engine/carddef.py:37-55`, mirrored by `CostModel` in `cards/schema.py:18-35`) carries exactly `mana`, `tap`, `untap`, `sacrifice`, `discard`, `discard_selector`, `discard_self`, `pay_life`, `remove_counters` and `exile_from_graveyard`; nothing in that list moves a battlefield permanent to hand. `sacrifice` is the closest -- same selector shape, same ask-the-player payment -- but it puts the land in the graveyard instead of the hand, which makes a materially different card: Meloku is played as a repeatable engine precisely because the lands come back and can be replayed, and a sacrifice version would strip-mine its own mana base. Substituting it would silently change the card. The `return_to_hand` **op** is in the vocabulary but is an effect, not a cost: effects run on resolution, so the ability could be activated with no land on the battlefield at all, the payment would not gate activation, and it would not be rewindable if it failed. Same need already filed under this slug for Trench Behemoth (`data/authoring/gaps/trench_behemoth.json`), whose ability has no mana component; one cost field satisfying both is the work item.

needs.what: a 1/1 blue flying Illusion token in the shared token pool -- one new object in `data/cards/tokens.cards.json`, following the naming already used there for keyworded tokens (`knight_2_2_w_vigilance`, `vampire_1_1_b_lifelink`): id `illusion_1_1_u_flying`, name `Illusion Token`, `types: ["Creature"]`, `subtypes: ["Illusion"]`, `colors: ["U"]`, `power: 1`, `toughness: 1`, `keywords: ["flying"]`, `is_token: true`, no mana cost. Every piece of that is already supported -- `flying` is in the keyword vocabulary and `knight_2_2_w_vigilance` proves a token may carry one -- so this is a data addition with no engine change behind it. With it in the pool the effect half is spelled `{"op": "create_token", "token": "illusion_1_1_u_flying", "amount": {"const": 1}}` and needs no new op.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `create_token` is in the vocabulary and can name any token id, but `validate_token_references` (`cards/loader.py:703-711`) raises `DslError: create_token references unknown card` for any id not already in the registry, and the whole pool today is 16 objects, none of them an Illusion and none of them a 1/1 blue flier: the only blue creature tokens are `komas_coil_3_3_u` and `kraken_8_8_u`, and the only 1/1 fliers are none at all. `create_token_copy` cannot stand in either -- it names no token id, so it can only copy something already on the battlefield, and nothing in Meloku's text copies anything. There is no facility for a card to define a token inline, so the token must exist as data before the card can load.
